title: mecardonia procumbens var. herniarioides
intro: Mecardonia procumbens var. herniarioides, commonly known as Creeping Jenny, is a type of flowering plant that belongs to the Plantaginaceae family. It is a prostrate herb native to Mexico and parts of the United States, with long, trailing stems and small, yellow or greenish-yellow flowers. The plant has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, due to its therapeutic actions, which include anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and expectorant properties. The bioactive constituents of Creeping Jenny include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which may contribute to its health benefits and medicinal uses.
